paper_metadata.title: VaR Estimation with Quantum Computing Noise Correction Using Neural Networks

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum VaR estimator that uses a tail-window state-preparation circuit on 4 qubits in simulation and 5 qubits on IBM Lagos, with a reported simulator VaR of USD -9111.50 and a real-device corrected estimate of USD 1376 for a 5-asset training case. Classical baselines remain central: the paper reports a 3-asset Monte Carlo VaR of USD -1219, a parametric VaR of USD -1213, and a linear-approximation error of 1.5% (improving to 0.22% with second-order Taylor terms), while the 138-asset portfolio is handled classically via the linear method.

experiments.description: Quantum circuit for VaR estimation using a distribution-window state-preparation approach, evaluated first on a statevector simulator and then on a real IBM quantum device; neural-network tuning is used to mitigate noise in the real-device run.

algorithm.variant: Qiskit state-preparation circuit for Gaussian-tail sampling with neural-network-tuned rotation angles

hyperparameters.qubits: 4 qubits in simulator example; 5 qubits in real-device example
hyperparameters.assets: 138 assets in the main portfolio example; 5 assets in the neural-network training example
hyperparameters.shots_or_repetitions: typically 1024 executions for quantum programs; paper also mentions 1000 to 2000 times for real-device execution
hyperparameters.activation: ReLU bounded to π / sigmoid alternative discussed

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial qubit rotations are random for the first epoch; neural network learns rotation parameters from training data

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A Qiskit state-preparation circuit maps a discretized interval of the Gaussian tail to computational basis states; the circuit uses rotation and CNOT gates to prepare amplitudes corresponding to probabilities in the VaR tail window.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the 1% VaR by sampling the tail of a Gaussian approximation to portfolio loss and mapping the measured percentile back to the VaR axis.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Windowing of the CDF tail to [−3σ, −2σ] and rescaling of the confidence level from α to β to focus limited qubits on the relevant tail region.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio VaR estimation for financial assets; main empirical example uses a 138-asset portfolio from a Peruvian financial institution, with a smaller 3-asset illustrative example and a 5-asset training example for the neural-network correction stage.

dataset_specification.description: Historical asset series from a financial institution; 80-day series for the 3-asset example; six months of data for the 138-asset portfolio; 5-asset dataset used for training/validation of the neural network

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute day-to-day increments, covariance matrix, Cholesky factorization; linear approximation via Taylor expansion; for quantum circuit, restrict to Gaussian tail window [−3σ, −2σ] and rescale confidence level; neural-network training uses grouped assets and cross-validation with all values except one
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against parametric VaR and classical Monte Carlo; simulator vs real-device histogram comparison; neural-network output validated against target VaR (e.g., 1380 USD target, 1376 USD estimated)

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: neural-network tuning of qubit rotation angles to compensate for noise

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Covariance and Cholesky computation; linear approximation; grouping assets; train/validation split; parametric VaR used as target for training
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Histogram processing to extract percentile and map it back to VaR; comparison to parametric VaR

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup is claimed; the paper positions the method as a NISQ-era noise-mitigated VaR estimation approach.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 5 qubits on IBM Lagos; 4-qubit simulator example; 1024 shots typical, with 1000-2000 repetitions mentioned for real-device runs
limiting_factors: No asymptotic quantum speedup is shown
Classical baselines (parametric and linear approximation) are competitive or better in accuracy and simplicity
Noise on the real device materially distorts the histogram
Only 4-5 qubits are used, far below problem sizes needed for finance advantage
The method relies on classical preprocessing and neural-network tuning

notes: The paper explicitly reports a 5-qubit real-device experiment on IBM Lagos and a 4-qubit simulator example; this entry consolidates the main quantum experiment and the real-device validation.
Circuit depth is not numerically reported; only the presence of rotation and CNOT gates is shown in the figure, so depth is left null and marked inferred/unknown.
No asymptotic quantum speedup is claimed; the paper positions the method as noise-mitigated VaR estimation on current NISQ hardware.
The authors present the method as a NISQ-oriented VaR estimator and do not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.
The paper explicitly compares against classical Monte Carlo and parametric estimation, with the classical methods remaining strong baselines.

experiments.description: Statevector-simulator evaluation of the same VaR distribution-window circuit for tail sampling and percentile extraction.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not reported; circuit generated from probability distribution using Qiskit state-preparation libraries

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution is clipped to a tail window and encoded into amplitudes via uniformly controlled rotations and CNOTs.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR from the 1% tail of the loss distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Tail-window clipping and rescaling of the percentile parameter.

problem_instance.description: Illustrative 138-asset portfolio example used to compute σ and define the tail window; simulator output shown for the 4-qubit circuit.

dataset_specification.description: Same portfolio as the main case study; simulator output compared to parametric VaR of USD −9514.18

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing as main experiment: covariance, Cholesky, linear approximation, tail-window selection
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector output compared to parametric estimation and to the real-device output

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Scale the measured basis state to obtain VaR estimate

speedup_claims.caveats: Simulator validation only; no speedup claim is made.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4-qubit statevector simulation of a tail-window state-preparation circuit
limiting_factors: Only a small illustrative circuit is shown
Classical postprocessing is required to map the measured state back to VaR

notes: The paper explicitly states the StatevectorSimulator and 4 qubits for the example circuit.

experiments.description: Classical baseline experiments used throughout the paper: Monte Carlo VaR estimation, parametric VaR estimation, and linear approximation to Monte Carlo (Taylor-series-based) for portfolios up to 138 assets.

algorithm.variant: Monte Carlo, parametric estimation, and linear approximation

hyperparameters.assets: 3-asset illustrative example; 5-asset training example; 138-asset portfolio case
hyperparameters.iterations: 1000 iterations in the 3-asset Monte Carlo example; tens of millions mentioned for full Monte Carlo generation

key_results: 138-asset portfolio handled with linear approximation plus Cheng/Higham-modified Cholesky
